raw_response:
I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the whole year, spread labor across seasons, and make sure I have a stable harvest. I do not have much room to gamble on specialty crops, and with my age and limited schooling, I would rather grow what I know well, what local buyers always take, and what fits the local water and weather conditions. So I will plant winter wheat on my full area through the cold season, harvest it in early summer, and then follow immediately with summer maize on the same land. I will use improved seed because I want steady yield and better resistance than old saved seed, but I will avoid management that is too complicated. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive amounts, because fertilizer is expensive and too much can lodge the wheat or waste money. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat here depends more on timely watering, especially at jointing and grain filling. I will keep pesticide use limited to what is needed, because I want to control pests and disease without spending more than the crop can return. For tillage, I will rotary till because it is practical, common locally, and easier for me than deep ploughing every time.
